title: Generations
subtitle: Talk about ageing, youth, and the ties between generations without stereotyping

lessons.title: Le vieillissement de la population
lessons.description: Describe France's ageing population with precise statistics, attributed sources, and demographic vocabulary.

blocks.heading: Une population qui vieillit : les chiffres clés
blocks.body: 'Le vieillissement de la population' describes a demographic shift, not an individual getting older — B2 French keeps the two senses distinct with different words: 'vieillir' (to age, for a person or a population) versus 'le vieillissement' (the process, as a noun). Precise description leans on 'l'espérance de vie' (life expectancy) and 'la natalité' (the birth rate) as the two figures that explain why a population's age structure shifts, and on naming a source before quoting a number.

examples.french: La population française vieillit, mais moins vite que celle de ses voisins européens.
examples.english: The French population is ageing, but more slowly than its European neighbours'.

examples.french: L'espérance de vie a augmenté de vingt ans depuis 1950.
examples.english: Life expectancy has increased by twenty years since 1950.

examples.french: Le taux de natalité recule depuis plusieurs décennies.
examples.english: The birth rate has been falling for several decades.

examples.french: Selon l'INSEE, un habitant sur quatre aura plus de soixante-cinq ans en 2050.
examples.english: According to INSEE, one in four residents will be over sixty-five in 2050.

examples.french: Le vieillissement n'est pas propre à la France : il touche presque toute l'Europe.
examples.english: Ageing is not unique to France: it affects almost all of Europe.

blocks.tip: 'L'INSEE' (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques) is the source French speakers name by default for population figures — citing it signals a serious, checkable claim.

blocks.heading: Actifs et retraités : un équilibre qui change
blocks.body: Demographic description at B2 distinguishes 'les actifs' (people of working age, in or seeking employment) from 'les retraités' (retirees), because the ratio between the two groups drives the funding debate around 'la retraite' and 'les cotisations' (payroll contributions). 'Le renouvellement générationnel' names the process by which new working-age adults replace those who retire — when it slows, fewer active contributors support more pensions, a purely descriptive fact that this lesson states without arguing for a particular fix.

examples.french: Le nombre d'actifs pour un retraité a fortement diminué depuis les années 1960.
examples.english: The number of working-age people per retiree has fallen sharply since the 1960s.

examples.french: Les cotisations des actifs financent en grande partie les pensions actuelles.
examples.english: Contributions from workers largely fund current pensions.

examples.french: Le renouvellement générationnel ralentit à mesure que la natalité baisse.
examples.english: Generational renewal is slowing as the birth rate falls.

examples.french: Le financement du système de retraite reste un sujet régulièrement débattu.
examples.english: Funding the pension system remains a regularly debated topic.

examples.french: Une politique publique peut chercher à relever le taux de natalité ou l'âge de la retraite.
examples.english: A public policy may try to raise the birth rate or the retirement age.

blocks.tip: 'Un actif' names a person by economic status (working-age, employed or job-seeking), not by age alone — a twenty-year-old student is not yet 'un actif'.

blocks.heading: Vivre plus longtemps : autonomie, dépendance, EHPAD
blocks.body: Longer lives raise a separate, more personal question this lesson also names carefully: how someone lives once daily tasks become harder. 'L'autonomie' (independence) is the default and the goal; 'la dépendance' (needing regular help) is a possible later stage, not an assumption about every older person. 'Un aidant' supports a family member at home; 'une maison de retraite' or, more specifically, 'un EHPAD' (a medicalised care home) is one option among several — never presented here as the only outcome of ageing.

examples.french: La grande majorité des personnes âgées vivent chez elles, en pleine autonomie.
examples.english: The vast majority of older people live at home, fully independent.

examples.french: La dépendance touche surtout les personnes de plus de quatre-vingt-cinq ans.
examples.english: Dependency mainly affects people over eighty-five.

examples.french: Un aidant familial accompagne souvent un parent sans formation ni salaire.
examples.english: A family caregiver often supports a relative with no training or pay.

examples.french: Un EHPAD propose un suivi médical que le domicile ne peut pas toujours offrir.
examples.english: A care home offers medical monitoring that home care cannot always provide.

examples.french: L'isolement, plus que l'âge lui-même, aggrave souvent la perte d'autonomie.
examples.english: Isolation, more than age itself, often worsens the loss of independence.

blocks.tip: Say 'une personne âgée' or 'un senior', never 'un vieux' — the descriptive register of this lesson avoids the informal, sometimes dismissive term entirely.

blocks.heading: Décrire une évolution chiffrée : augmenter de, atteindre, représenter
blocks.body: Precise demographic description at B2 pairs a variation verb with an exact quantity: 'augmenter/diminuer de + [amount]' states a change, 'atteindre + [figure]' states an endpoint, and 'représenter + [percentage]' states a share of a whole. Keep the preposition 'de' before the amount when describing change ('augmenter de six ans'), and never insert it before a straight destination figure ('atteindre 30 %', not 'atteindre à 30 %').

examples.french: L'espérance de vie a augmenté de six ans en trente ans.
examples.english: Life expectancy has increased by six years in thirty years.

examples.french: Le taux de natalité a diminué de deux points depuis 2010.
examples.english: The birth rate has fallen by two points since 2010.

examples.french: La part des plus de soixante-cinq ans devrait atteindre trente pour cent en 2070.
examples.english: The share of over-sixty-fives should reach thirty percent in 2070.

examples.french: Les retraités représentent aujourd'hui près d'un quart de la population.
examples.english: Retirees today account for nearly a quarter of the population.

blocks.tip: 'Un point' (a percentage point) is not the same as 'un pour cent' — going from 20 % to 22 % is a rise of two points, not two percent, and mixing them up undermines a precise claim.

blocks.heading: La nominalisation : donner un ton factuel et neutre
blocks.body: Formal, descriptive French often turns a verb or adjective into a noun to sound more neutral and report-like: 'vieillir' becomes 'le vieillissement', 'augmenter' becomes 'une augmentation', 'dépendant' becomes 'la dépendance'. A nominalised sentence removes the subject doing the action and centres the phenomenon itself — useful when describing a trend rather than blaming or crediting anyone for it.

examples.french: La population vieillit. → Le vieillissement de la population s'accélère.
examples.english: The population is ageing. → The ageing of the population is accelerating.

examples.french: Le nombre de naissances diminue. → La diminution des naissances inquiète les experts.
examples.english: The number of births is decreasing. → The decrease in births worries experts.

examples.french: Les gens vivent plus longtemps. → L'allongement de la vie change les besoins en santé.
examples.english: People live longer. → The lengthening of life changes health needs.

examples.french: On finance les retraites. → Le financement des retraites reste un sujet sensible.
examples.english: Pensions are financed. → The funding of pensions remains a sensitive topic.

blocks.tip: A nominalised noun phrase almost always needs 'de' before what follows: 'le vieillissement de la population', not 'le vieillissement la population' — the 'de' carries the relationship the verb used to express directly.

passages.title: Sainte-Colombe, un village qui vieillit
passages.french:
Sainte-Colombe compte environ neuf cents habitants, nichés entre deux collines du Limousin.
Selon la mairie, l'âge moyen y a augmenté de douze ans en trente ans.
La boulangère, Claire Dubosc, l'observe chaque matin derrière son comptoir.
« Autrefois, l'école accueillait quatre-vingts enfants ; aujourd'hui, ils sont vingt-deux », explique-t-elle.
La natalité recule, tandis que l'espérance de vie continue de progresser.
Beaucoup de jeunes actifs sont partis travailler à Limoges ou à Bordeaux.
Ceux qui restent sont, pour la plupart, retraités ou proches de la retraite.
Cela ne signifie pas que le village décline : il se transforme.
Un cabinet médical a ouvert pour répondre aux besoins d'une population vieillissante.
Une association propose des activités pour lutter contre l'isolement.
La mairie a aussi financé un service de transport pour les personnes à mobilité réduite.
« La dépendance ne concerne qu'une minorité de nos aînés », rappelle Claire Dubosc.
« La plupart restent chez eux, autonomes, jusqu'à un âge avancé. »
Selon elle, le vrai défi n'est pas l'âge, mais l'isolement que crée un village qui se vide.
Sainte-Colombe cherche donc à attirer de nouveaux actifs, pas seulement à accompagner ses seniors.
passages.english:
Sainte-Colombe has about nine hundred residents, nestled between two hills in the Limousin.
According to the town hall, the average age there has risen by twelve years in thirty years.
The baker, Claire Dubosc, observes it every morning behind her counter.
"The school used to welcome eighty children; today there are twenty-two," she explains.
The birth rate is falling, while life expectancy continues to rise.
Many young working-age people have left to work in Limoges or Bordeaux.
Those who remain are, for the most part, retired or close to retirement.
That does not mean the village is declining: it is transforming.
A medical practice opened to meet the needs of an ageing population.
An association offers activities to fight isolation.
The town hall also funded a transport service for people with reduced mobility.
"Dependency affects only a minority of our elders," Claire Dubosc notes.
"Most stay at home, independent, until an advanced age."
According to her, the real challenge is not age but the isolation created by an emptying village.
Sainte-Colombe is therefore trying to attract new working-age residents, not just support its seniors.

Le coût des maisons de retraite
Le refus des jeunes de vieillir
questions.answer: L'isolement causé par un village qui se vide

lessons.title: Les jeunes aujourd'hui
lessons.description: Talk about young people today while avoiding sweeping generalisations — attribute views, cite sources, and nuance every claim.

blocks.heading: Le piège de la généralisation
blocks.body: 'Les jeunes' is not a single group with a single opinion, income, or habit — B2 French for this topic starts by naming the trap: 'généraliser' turns one example, or even a real trend, into a claim about an entire generation. The safer habit is to qualify the group ('certains jeunes', 'une partie des jeunes', 'les jeunes diplômés') rather than using the bare plural as if it spoke for everyone, and to mark any broad claim with a source instead of presenting it as self-evident.

examples.french: Dire « les jeunes ne travaillent pas » est une généralisation, pas une observation.
examples.english: Saying "young people don't work" is a generalisation, not an observation.

examples.french: Certains jeunes s'engagent énormément ; d'autres se tiennent à distance de la politique.
examples.english: Some young people get very involved; others keep their distance from politics.

examples.french: Une partie des jeunes diplômés peine à trouver un premier emploi stable.
examples.english: Some young graduates struggle to find a first stable job.

examples.french: Un cliché ne devient pas vrai parce qu'il est répété souvent.
examples.english: A cliché does not become true just because it is repeated often.

examples.french: Il faut nuancer : la situation varie énormément selon le milieu social et la région.
examples.english: This needs qualifying: the situation varies enormously by social background and region.

blocks.tip: Swap 'les jeunes' for 'de nombreux jeunes' or 'certains jeunes' whenever the claim that follows is not true of every young person — which is almost always.

blocks.heading: Attribuer un point de vue plutôt que l'affirmer
blocks.body: Since youth is a heavily discussed and often stereotyped topic, B2 description leans on attribution: 'selon un sondage', 'd'après une enquête', 'les jeunes interrogés déclarent que'. This keeps a claim tied to its evidence and its scope, and it separates a reported opinion from the speaker's own. It also allows two contradictory findings to sit side by side without either being presented as the final truth.

examples.french: Selon un sondage récent, la majorité des jeunes se disent inquiets pour le climat.
examples.english: According to a recent poll, most young people say they are worried about the climate.

examples.french: D'après cette enquête, l'engagement associatif progresse chez les moins de trente ans.
examples.english: According to this survey, volunteering is rising among under-thirties.

examples.french: Les jeunes interrogés déclarent vouloir un métier qui a du sens.
examples.english: The young people surveyed say they want a job that has meaning.

examples.french: Un autre sondage nuance ce constat et montre des priorités très diverses.
examples.english: Another poll nuances this finding and shows very diverse priorities.

examples.french: Ce témoignage reflète une expérience individuelle, pas une tendance générale.
examples.english: This account reflects an individual experience, not a general trend.

blocks.tip: 'Les jeunes interrogés' (the young people surveyed) is more honest than 'les jeunes' alone — it reminds the listener the claim covers only the people actually asked.

blocks.heading: Une génération face à la précarité et au numérique
blocks.body: Two real, sourced trends do come up often in this topic — youth unemployment and job insecurity ('le chômage des jeunes', 'la précarité') on one hand, and a life shaped by digital tools and social media on the other. B2 French presents both as documented facts with real consequences, not as verdicts on an entire generation's character: a young person's use of 'les réseaux sociaux' or a difficult 'insertion professionnelle' says something about the economy and the era, not about who they are.

examples.french: Le chômage des jeunes reste plus élevé que la moyenne nationale.
examples.english: Youth unemployment remains higher than the national average.

examples.french: La précarité touche particulièrement les premiers emplois et les stages.
examples.english: Job insecurity particularly affects first jobs and internships.

examples.french: Les réseaux sociaux occupent une place importante, sans pour autant définir toute une génération.
examples.english: Social media takes up an important place, without defining an entire generation.

examples.french: Beaucoup de jeunes militent pour le climat, sans que cela concerne tous les jeunes.
examples.english: Many young people campaign for the climate, without that applying to all young people.

examples.french: Le pouvoir d'achat des jeunes actifs reste un sujet d'inquiétude fréquent.
examples.english: The purchasing power of young workers remains a frequent concern.

blocks.tip: Explain a difficulty (precarious jobs, low pay) as a structural fact about the job market — never as evidence about young people's work ethic.

items.example: D'après cette enquête, l'engagement associatif progresse.
items.exampleEnglish: According to this survey, volunteering is rising.

items.exampleEnglish: One young person's opinion never represents their whole generation.

blocks.heading: Quantifier sans généraliser : certains, une partie de, la plupart de
blocks.body: Instead of the bare plural 'les jeunes', B2 French offers a scale of quantifiers that state exactly how much of a group a claim covers: 'certains jeunes' (some), 'une partie des jeunes' (a portion), 'la plupart des jeunes' (most, but not all), 'la majorité de' (the majority). Each phrase takes 'de' before the group and agrees the following verb with that group, not with the quantifier.

examples.french: Certains jeunes s'engagent dans une association dès le lycée.
examples.english: Some young people get involved in an association as early as high school.

examples.french: Une partie des jeunes actifs vit encore chez ses parents.
examples.english: A portion of young workers still lives with their parents.

examples.french: La plupart des jeunes interrogés disent vouloir un travail qui a du sens.
examples.english: Most of the young people surveyed say they want work that has meaning.

examples.french: La majorité des étudiants de cette enquête travaillent à côté de leurs études.
examples.english: The majority of students in this survey work alongside their studies.

blocks.tip: 'La plupart de' takes a plural verb ('la plupart des jeunes pensent'), while 'la majorité de' can take either — but stay consistent within the same paragraph.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel pour rapporter sans garantir
blocks.body: When repeating a finding you have not personally verified — a poll result, a claim made in the press — B2 French often shifts the verb into the conditional to mark the information as reported, not confirmed: 'les jeunes seraient plus engagés' (young people are said to be more involved) rather than the flat indicative 'les jeunes sont plus engagés'. This single tense shift does the work an entire sentence of hedging would otherwise need.

examples.french: Selon cette étude, les jeunes seraient de plus en plus engagés dans le bénévolat.
examples.english: According to this study, young people are said to be increasingly involved in volunteering.

examples.french: Le chômage des jeunes aurait légèrement baissé ce trimestre.
examples.english: Youth unemployment reportedly fell slightly this quarter.

examples.french: D'après le sondage, une majorité des jeunes se dirait inquiète pour l'avenir.
examples.english: According to the poll, a majority of young people are said to feel worried about the future.

examples.french: Les résultats définitifs ne seraient publiés qu'en fin d'année.
examples.english: The final results reportedly will not be published until the end of the year.

blocks.tip: Switch back to the plain indicative once you have checked and confirmed the figure yourself — the conditional signals 'reported', not 'permanently uncertain'.

passages.title: Trois portraits, une génération
passages.french:
Que pensent vraiment les jeunes ? La question paraît simple ; la réponse ne l'est pas.
Pour cet article, nous avons rencontré trois personnes de vingt-deux ans, à Nantes.
Inès termine des études d'ingénieure et milite chaque week-end pour le climat.
« Je ne me reconnais pas dans le mot “insouciant” qu'on colle souvent à ma génération », dit-elle.
Yanis, lui, enchaîne les stages depuis deux ans sans trouver de contrat stable.
« On me dit que les jeunes ne veulent pas travailler ; moi, je cherche surtout un poste qui existe encore dans cinq ans. »
Léa, enfin, a quitté la fac pour reprendre la boulangerie de son grand-père.
« Je passe plus de temps avec des clients de soixante-dix ans qu'avec des gens de mon âge », remarque-t-elle en riant.
Selon un sondage cité par l'article, la majorité des jeunes se disent inquiets pour le climat.
Mais d'après la même enquête, leurs priorités concrètes varient énormément selon le milieu et la région.
Certains jeunes s'engagent dans une association ; d'autres consacrent leur énergie à un premier emploi précaire.
Aucun de ces trois portraits ne résume les autres, et c'est précisément ce que montre ce reportage.
Inès, Yanis et Léa ont vingt-deux ans, la même ville, et des trajectoires presque opposées.
Généraliser à partir de l'un d'eux reviendrait à effacer les deux autres.
passages.english:
What do young people really think? The question seems simple; the answer is not.
For this article, we met three twenty-two-year-olds in Nantes.
Inès is finishing an engineering degree and campaigns for the climate every weekend.
"I don't recognise myself in the word 'carefree' that's often stuck onto my generation," she says.
Yanis, meanwhile, has gone through internship after internship for two years without finding a stable contract.
"People tell me young people don't want to work; I'm mainly looking for a job that will still exist in five years."
Léa, finally, left university to take over her grandfather's bakery.
"I spend more time with seventy-year-old customers than with people my own age," she notes, laughing.
According to a poll cited in the article, most young people say they are worried about the climate.
But according to the same survey, their concrete priorities vary enormously by background and region.
Some young people get involved in an association; others devote their energy to a precarious first job.
None of these three portraits sums up the others, and that is exactly what this report shows.
Inès, Yanis, and Léa are twenty-two, live in the same city, and have almost opposite paths.
Generalising from any one of them would mean erasing the other two.

lessons.title: Le lien intergénérationnel
lessons.description: Explore what different generations can offer each other, from shared know-how to mutual support, through everyday scenes rather than clichés.

blocks.heading: Ce que la transmission met en jeu
blocks.body: 'La transmission' names the passing on of something — a recipe, a skill, a way of speaking — from one generation to another, and B2 French treats it as a two-way process rather than a one-way gift from old to young. 'Le savoir-faire' (practical know-how) and 'la sagesse' (wisdom drawn from experience) travel down; curiosity about new tools, especially 'le numérique', often travels the other way. Naming both directions avoids reducing either generation to only a giver or only a receiver.

examples.french: La transmission ne va pas dans un seul sens : chacun apprend de l'autre.
examples.english: Passing things on does not go in only one direction: each learns from the other.

examples.french: Son grand-père lui a transmis un savoir-faire qu'aucun livre n'explique vraiment.
examples.english: Her grandfather passed on to her a know-how that no book really explains.

examples.french: Sa petite-fille, en retour, l'a initié aux appels vidéo.
examples.english: His granddaughter, in turn, introduced him to video calls.

examples.french: L'expérience d'un aîné et la curiosité d'un plus jeune se complètent souvent bien.
examples.english: An elder's experience and a younger person's curiosity often complement each other well.

examples.french: Le fossé générationnel se réduit quand chacun accepte d'apprendre de l'autre.
examples.english: The generational gap narrows when each is willing to learn from the other.

blocks.tip: Use 'transmettre à' for what an older generation passes on and 'initier à' for what a younger one introduces — both structures take 'à' before what is being taught.

blocks.heading: L'entraide au quotidien : bénévolat, aidants, colocation
blocks.body: Concrete intergenerational contact often takes organised forms worth naming precisely: 'le bénévolat' (volunteering) that pairs students with isolated seniors, 'un aidant' who supports an older relative, or 'la colocation intergénérationnelle' — a scheme where a student lives with an older person in exchange for company and a reduced rent. Each format involves 'l'entraide' (mutual help) and 'la solidarité', words that describe reciprocity rather than charity in one direction only.

examples.french: La colocation intergénérationnelle permet à une étudiante de vivre chez une personne âgée.
examples.english: Intergenerational flat-sharing lets a student live with an older person.

examples.french: En échange d'un loyer réduit, elle lui tient compagnie et l'aide avec son ordinateur.
examples.english: In exchange for reduced rent, she keeps her company and helps her with her computer.

examples.french: Le bénévolat auprès des personnes âgées lutte directement contre l'isolement.
examples.english: Volunteering with older people directly fights isolation.

examples.french: Un aidant familial reçoit parfois des conseils précieux de la personne qu'il accompagne.
examples.english: A family caregiver sometimes receives valuable advice from the person they support.

examples.french: L'entraide entre générations profite rarement à un seul camp.
examples.english: Mutual help between generations rarely benefits only one side.

blocks.tip: 'La colocation intergénérationnelle' is a specific, named housing arrangement in France — treat it as a concrete example, not a general metaphor for all contact between generations.

blocks.heading: Une complémentarité plutôt qu'une hiérarchie
blocks.body: B2 description of this topic resists ranking generations against each other: instead of 'les jeunes devraient écouter les anciens' (a hierarchy), it favours 'complémentarité' — each generation offers something distinct, and neither view alone is complete. 'Tisser un lien', 'enrichir', and 'le respect mutuel' describe a relationship built through shared activity, not a debt owed by one side to the other.

examples.french: Ce n'est pas une question de hiérarchie, mais de complémentarité.
examples.english: It is not a question of hierarchy, but of complementarity.

examples.french: Grand-parents et petits-enfants tissent un lien qui enrichit les deux côtés.
examples.english: Grandparents and grandchildren build a bond that enriches both sides.

examples.french: Le respect mutuel se construit par l'écoute, pas par l'âge.
examples.english: Mutual respect is built through listening, not through age.

examples.french: Un mentor apprend parfois autant qu'il n'enseigne.
examples.english: A mentor sometimes learns as much as they teach.

examples.french: Le patrimoine familial se transmet, mais il se réinvente aussi à chaque génération.
examples.english: Family heritage is passed on, but it is also reinvented with each generation.

blocks.tip: 'Complémentarité' is the keyword of this lesson — reach for it whenever a sentence risks implying that one generation simply teaches and the other simply obeys.

blocks.heading: Les pronoms compléments avec les verbes de transmission
blocks.body: Verbs like 'transmettre à', 'apprendre à', and 'initier à' take an indirect object (the person receiving) and often a direct object (the thing passed on) at once, so both slots need a pronoun when the nouns are dropped: 'lui' for the person, 'le/la/les' for the thing. Word order in a positive sentence is direct-object pronoun before the indirect: 'Elle le lui a appris' (She taught it to him).

examples.french: Sa grand-mère lui a transmis sa recette de tarte aux pommes.
examples.english: Her grandmother passed her apple tart recipe on to her.

examples.french: Elle la lui a transmise avec beaucoup de patience.
examples.english: She passed it on to her with a lot of patience.

examples.french: Son petit-fils lui apprend à utiliser un smartphone.
examples.english: Her grandson is teaching her to use a smartphone.

examples.french: Il le lui a appris en une seule après-midi.
examples.english: He taught it to her in a single afternoon.

blocks.tip: The past participle agrees with a preceding direct object pronoun: 'transmise' takes an 'e' because 'la' (the recipe, feminine) comes before the verb.

blocks.heading: Le gérondif : deux actions en même temps
blocks.body: 'En + present participle' (the gérondif) describes two things happening at once — often exactly the kind of everyday, side-by-side moment where transmission actually occurs: 'en cuisinant', 'en discutant', 'en regardant'. It is more compact than 'pendant que' and keeps both generations as active participants in the same sentence rather than one teaching and one merely listening.

examples.french: Sa grand-mère lui raconte l'histoire de la famille en cuisinant.
examples.english: Her grandmother tells her the family's history while cooking.

examples.french: Ils apprennent l'un de l'autre en discutant chaque dimanche.
examples.english: They learn from each other by talking every Sunday.

examples.french: En l'aidant avec son ordinateur, elle a découvert son sens de l'humour.
examples.english: While helping him with his computer, she discovered his sense of humour.

examples.french: On tisse souvent un lien en partageant une activité, pas en s'y forçant.
examples.english: A bond is often built by sharing an activity, not by forcing it.

blocks.tip: The gérondif's subject must match the main clause's subject — 'en cuisinant, elle raconte' works because 'elle' is doing both the cooking and the telling.

passages.title: Marcel et Inès, colocataires
passages.french:
Marcel a quatre-vingt-deux ans et vit seul depuis la mort de sa femme, il y a six ans.
Depuis septembre, une chambre de son appartement accueille Inès, étudiante en architecture.
Le principe est simple : un loyer réduit, en échange d'un peu de compagnie et d'un coup de main.
Au début, Marcel craignait le bruit et la musique ; Inès craignait l'ennui et le silence.
Aucun des deux préjugés ne s'est vraiment confirmé.
Le mardi soir, Marcel lui apprend à faire son fameux gratin dauphinois.
Le jeudi, Inès l'initie aux appels vidéo pour qu'il puisse voir ses arrière-petits-enfants à Lyon.
« Elle m'a redonné une raison de sortir de mon fauteuil », dit Marcel en riant.
Inès, elle, apprécie surtout les histoires qu'il raconte sur le quartier d'avant.
« Il connaît chaque immeuble, chaque commerçant depuis cinquante ans », explique-t-elle.
Cette colocation intergénérationnelle n'efface pas leurs différences : ils ne regardent pas les mêmes séries.
Mais elle a créé un lien réel, fait d'écoute autant que d'entraide.
Ce n'est pas une question de hiérarchie, l'un enseignant et l'autre apprenant.
C'est une complémentarité, où chacun donne et reçoit à son tour.
passages.english:
Marcel is eighty-two and has lived alone since his wife died six years ago.
Since September, a room in his flat has been home to Inès, an architecture student.
The arrangement is simple: reduced rent, in exchange for some company and a helping hand.
At first, Marcel feared noise and music; Inès feared boredom and silence.
Neither prejudice was really confirmed.
On Tuesday evenings, Marcel teaches her to make his famous gratin dauphinois.
On Thursdays, Inès introduces him to video calls so he can see his great-grandchildren in Lyon.
"She gave me a reason to get out of my armchair again," Marcel says, laughing.
Inès, for her part, mostly enjoys the stories he tells about the neighbourhood of the past.
"He knows every building, every shopkeeper, for fifty years back," she explains.
This intergenerational flat-share does not erase their differences: they do not watch the same shows.
But it has created a real bond, made of listening as much as mutual help.
It is not a question of hierarchy, with one teaching and the other learning.
It is a complementarity, where each gives and receives in turn.
